audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 4, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for administrative hierarchy, regional provisioning, royal marriages, tribute, imperial reach, court consumption, animal systems, militarization, public security, wisdom claims, and knowledge of creation.

verses.restored: King Solomon was king over all Israel.
These were officials he had: Azariah son of Zadok, the priest;
Elihoreph and Ahijah sons of Shisha, scribes; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud, recorder.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over army; Zadok and Abiathar were priests.
Azariah son of Nathan was over administrators; Zabud son of Nathan was priest/chief official and king's friend.
Ahishar was over household; Adoniram son of Abda was over forced labor/tribute.
Solomon had twelve administrators over all Israel. They provided food for king and his household; each provided for one month in year.
These are their names: Ben-hur in hill country of Ephraim;
Ben-deker in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh, and Elon-beth-hanan;
Ben-hesed in Arubboth; Socoh and all land of Hepher were his.
Ben-abinadab in all heights/region of Dor; Taphath daughter of Solomon was his wife.
Baana son of Ahilud had Taanach, Megiddo, and all Beth-shean beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah and beyond Jokmeam.
Ben-geber was in Ramoth-gilead; towns of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead were his, and region of Argob in Bashan—sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars.
Ahinadab son of Iddo was in Mahanaim.
Ahimaaz was in Naphtali; he also took Basemath daughter of Solomon as wife.
Baana son of Hushai was in Asher and Bealoth.
Jehoshaphat son of Paruah was in Issachar.
Shimei son of Ela was in Benjamin.
Geber son of Uri was in land of Gilead, land of Sihon king of Amorites and Og king of Bashan; one administrator was over land.
Judah and Israel were many, like sand beside sea in multitude, eating, drinking, and rejoicing.
Solomon ruled over all kingdoms from River to land of Philistines and border of Egypt. They brought tribute and served Solomon all days of his life.
Solomon's provision for one day was thirty kors of fine flour and sixty kors of meal,
ten fattened cattle, twenty pasture-fed cattle, one hundred sheep, besides deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened birds.
He had dominion over all beyond River, from Tiphsah to Gaza, over all kings beyond River, and had peace from every side around him.
Judah and Israel lived in security, each under vine and fig tree, from Dan to Beersheba, all days of Solomon.
Solomon had forty thousand stalls of horses for chariots and twelve thousand horsemen.
Those administrators provided food for King Solomon and all who came to king's table, each in his month; they let nothing be lacking.
They brought barley and straw for horses and swift steeds to required place, each according to his charge.
Divine gave Solomon very great wisdom and understanding, and breadth of heart like sand upon seashore.
Solomon's wisdom was greater than wisdom of all children of east and all wisdom of Egypt.
He was wiser than every human—than Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Calcol, and Darda, sons of Mahol—and his name/fame was among all nations around.
He spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs were one thousand and five.
He spoke concerning trees, from cedar in Lebanon to hyssop growing from wall. He spoke concerning animals, birds, creeping things, and fish.
People came from all peoples to hear wisdom of Solomon, from all kings of earth who heard his wisdom.

translation_notes: The administrative list is not neutral bureaucracy. It maps who collects food, labor, and resources for the palace and who supervises the people doing that work.
Adoniram's portfolio over forced labor/tribute anticipates the grievance that fractures the kingdom. Administrative efficiency can institutionalize exploitation.
Taphath and Basemath, Solomon's daughters, appear through marriages to regional officials. Their consent and political roles are not recorded.
The image of each person under vine and fig tree preserves a genuine ideal of ordinary security, but it exists beside tribute, imperial service, enormous palace consumption, and military buildup.
Daily court provisions and animal numbers reflect concentrated wealth and extraction. Abundance at the royal table does not prove abundance in every household.
The empire's peoples bring gifts/tribute and serve Solomon. 'Peace' may describe absence of revolt from the center while conquered communities experience domination.
Wisdom includes poetry and close observation of plants and animals. Knowledge of creation must not be confused with ownership or permission to exploit it.
Comparisons that make Solomon wiser than whole regions risk civilizational superiority. Egypt and eastern peoples possess their own wisdom traditions and human dignity.
safety_note: Do not romanticize the administrative machine, tribute, forced labor, militarization, or extravagant court consumption as proof of Divine prosperity. Test royal wisdom by whether ordinary people, workers, neighboring peoples, and animals flourish.
